title: Sea Fig: Ancient Sea Figs You Can Visit
meta_description: A strangler fig that stops at southern Kyushu: Kagoshima's volcano-side akou, said to near a thousand years, and Nojima Shrine's lone designated tree.
intro: Ficus superba is a strangler fig from the edge of the subtropics, and it stops almost exactly where these three trees stand. Its range runs up from Taiwan and the Ryukyus and gives out around southern Kyushu, which is why nobody further north has heard of one and why Kagoshima alone protects four by name. The oldest sits on the side of an active volcano: the city's own signboard puts it near a thousand years, a figure three times the next-oldest tree on the register and resting on no published method, so take it as an official estimate rather than a measurement. At Nojima Shrine on the Nichinan coast, akou figs pour their roots over walls and rock through the whole precinct, and almost every visitor assumes the entire grove is protected; only one tree there actually carries the 1941 national designation. Three mapped so far, across two cities.
